incidents.vector: Breach of a government agency that manages healthcare entitlements; method not yet disclosed.
incidents.impact: Personal information of more than 67 million Thai citizens allegedly stolen, with portions of the data posted to online criminal markets. The Thai government has launched an investigation.

incidents.vector: Compromise of the lawmaker's Signal messaging account; the FBI notified him of the breach.
incidents.impact: Suspected Russian hackers accessed the Signal account of Rep. Don Bacon, a Nebraska Republican and vocal Ukraine supporter and Kremlin critic, in an apparent intelligence-collection operation against a U.S. official.

incidents.vector: Data breach traced back to a Chinese software engineer who has since left South Korea; access details not fully disclosed.
incidents.impact: A 2025 breach exposed the personal information of 34 million customers, leading South Korea's privacy regulator to impose a record $409 million fine. Coupang says it will appeal.

incidents.victim: Higher education sector (100+ orgs; University of Nottingham confirmed)
incidents.vector: Mass exploitation of an unauthenticated Oracle PeopleSoft PeopleTools zero-day (CVE-2026-35273) in the Environment Management Hub, used to gain remote code execution, deploy MeshCentral C2, spray SSH credentials, and exfiltrate data with zstd compression.
incidents.impact: The ShinyHunters gang claims to have compromised 300+ PeopleSoft instances across 100+ organizations (68% of them universities); the University of Nottingham confirmed theft of ~455,000 records and 40GB of student data including passport numbers and payment details. Victims are being actively extorted on a dark-web leak site.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of a maximum-severity OS command-injection flaw (CVE-2026-10520, CVSS 10) in Ivanti Sentry mobile gateways, using a public proof-of-concept within 24 hours of disclosure to gain unauthenticated root code execution.
incidents.impact: Shadowserver observed widespread exploitation attempts and at least two backdoored instances; attackers appeared to have pre-mapped Ivanti's exposed assets. Compromise grants control of appliance configurations, stored credentials, and directory connections.

incidents.victim: Check Point Security Gateway / VPN customers
incidents.vector: Exploitation of a critical authentication-bypass zero-day (CVE-2026-50751, CVSS 9.3) in Check Point Remote Access VPN / Mobile Access using deprecated IKEv1, letting attackers establish a VPN session without valid credentials.
incidents.impact: Exploited in the wild since at least May 7 against a few dozen organizations globally; Check Point confirmed at least one case of post-exploitation activity tied to a financially motivated Qilin ransomware affiliate. Added to CISA's KEV catalog.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack on operational systems; the company has not disclosed whether ransomware or data theft was involved.
incidents.impact: Australia's second-largest sugar producer shut down its Farleigh and Racecourse mills in Queensland, halting cane haulage and milling at the start of the crushing season and forcing growers to stop harvesting.

incidents.vector: Abuse of an API bug to access data from ServiceNow customer instances; reportedly exploited since at least April before ServiceNow quietly patched it.
incidents.impact: Attackers accessed data from customer instances, primarily affecting customers on ServiceNow's Australia platform release. The company has notified affected customers.

incidents.victim: Current and former U.S. security clearance holders
incidents.vector: Network of 13 fake 'consulting' company websites using AI-generated photos, fictitious personas, and encrypted apps to lure clearance holders into selling sensitive or classified information for cash.
incidents.impact: The DOJ and FBI seized 13 internet domains used by suspected Chinese intelligence agents since November 2023 to recruit current and former U.S. government and military employees with access to classified information.

incidents.vector: Website intrusion to delete articles and disrupt broadcasts; attackers also threatened to dox and harm employees.
incidents.impact: The pro-Iran Handala group breached the independent all-female news agency's website, deleted articles, and disrupted its online broadcasts as part of intimidation of journalists.

incidents.victim: U.S. critical infrastructure / past Conti victims
incidents.vector: Conti ransomware deployed against 1,000+ organizations; member Oleksii Lytvynenko developed malware and held stolen data from 12 victims.
incidents.impact: A longtime Conti member pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit wire fraud and faces up to 20 years; the FBI estimates Conti extorted more than $150 million before disbanding in 2022 and splintering into successor groups (Black Basta, Royal, BlackSuit).

incidents.vector: A CISA contractor intentionally published AWS GovCloud keys and a large trove of agency secrets to a public GitHub account, exposing credentials to anyone.
incidents.impact: The exposure prompted a congressional inquiry; CISA is still struggling to contain the breach and invalidate the leaked credentials, raising risk of follow-on intrusions into federal systems.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of a validation-error zero-day (CVE-2026-20245) in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager allowing command injection and execution of commands as root; exploitation may chain earlier Cisco zero-days for initial access.
incidents.impact: The seventh actively exploited Cisco SD-WAN zero-day this year. Cisco observed limited cases where exploitation pushed configuration changes to edge devices; no patch was available at disclosure and there are no workarounds.

incidents.victim: U.S. legal, professional and financial services firms (incl. Weil Gotshal & Manges)
incidents.vector: Voice phishing (vishing) and IT-helpdesk impersonation to trick employees into screen-sharing and installing remote-access tools; in some cases attackers physically entered offices posing as IT staff and used USB devices to steal data.
incidents.impact: The Silent Ransom Group (UNC3753 / Luna Moth) hit dozens of organizations between January and May 2026, moving from access to extortion in under an hour in some cases. Law firm Weil Gotshal & Manges reportedly paid an estimated $20 million to prevent release of stolen client data.

incidents.vector: Spear-phishing campaign luring targeted WhatsApp users to click malicious links leading to an external site, in apparent violation of a U.S. court injunction barring NSO from targeting WhatsApp.
incidents.impact: Meta says it found and disrupted a new NSO Group operation targeting WhatsApp users and filed a contempt motion; the case underscores continued commercial-spyware targeting of high-value individuals.

incidents.victim: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS GlobalProtect customers
incidents.vector: Exploitation of an authentication-bypass flaw (CVE-2026-0257) in PAN-OS GlobalProtect; attackers forge authentication-override cookies using the appliance's public TLS certificate to establish VPN sessions without credentials.
incidents.impact: Initially rated medium then reassessed as critical after active exploitation in two waves (from May 17) across numerous customer environments. Some attackers obtained internal network access; activity assessed as opportunistic initial access. Added to CISA's KEV catalog.

incidents.victim: Red Hat (npm package ecosystem) and downstream developers
incidents.vector: Compromise of a Red Hat employee GitHub account and the upstream CI/CD pipeline to push trojanized packages with valid SLSA provenance; an npm preinstall hook ran a 4.29MB dropper ('Miasma', a Mini Shai-Hulud worm variant) that harvested cloud, GitHub, npm, and Vault credentials and self-propagated.
incidents.impact: 32 maliciously modified @redhat-cloud-services packages (90+ versions, ~80,000-117,000 weekly downloads) distributed credential-stealing malware to developers before removal. Part of an ongoing wave of self-replicating npm/PyPI supply-chain worms; Microsoft also reported 72 of its Azure Durable Task SDK repos hit by a related worm.

incidents.victim: Instagram accounts (Obama White House, U.S. Space Force)
incidents.vector: Social engineering of Meta's AI support assistant: using a VPN near the target's location, attackers requested a password reset and tricked the bot into linking the account to an attacker email, which received a one-time reset code (defeated only where MFA was enabled).
incidents.impact: Pro-Iran hackers briefly defaced the Instagram accounts of the Obama White House and the Chief Master Sergeant of the U.S. Space Force with pro-Iranian messaging and hijacked valuable short account names. Meta pushed an emergency patch; no backend database was breached.

incidents.victim: EU targets (via Stark Industries / MIRhosting infrastructure)
incidents.vector: Bulletproof hosting providers (the[.]hosting / WorkTitans / MIRhosting, successors to EU-sanctioned Stark Industries Solutions) supplied IT infrastructure for Russian DDoS, influence, and disinformation operations against EU targets.
incidents.impact: Dutch financial-crime investigators arrested the co-owners of two related hosting firms and seized 800+ servers; the networks were the most-used in pro-Russian attacks on Danish government bodies around the November 2025 municipal elections.
